name: Tensyl-X
description: Tensyl-X is a ultra-high tensile strength CNT cable material produced through quantum-aligned axial growth, where individual nanotubes are grown in perfect parallel orientation across macro-scale lengths — eliminating the tube-to-tube slip that limited earlier CNT cables. The result is a material with tensile strength exceeding 120 GPa, roughly sixty times that of high-grade steel at one-sixth the weight. Apex Nanofabrication produces it in continuous spooled filament, braided cable, and flat ribbon formats, making it the dominant structural cable material in aerospace, megastructure construction, and high-load augment anchoring.
applications: winch and rigging systems for heavy salvage
cost: Φ420 per kg (raw filament); Φ1,100 per kg (braided cable assembly)
story_hooks: A Tensyl-X spool goes missing from an Apex Nanofabrication shipment — enough cable to suspend a building, or to rig something catastrophic. The manifest shows it was signed out by an employee who died three weeks ago.

A runner's prosthetic arm fails catastrophically mid-job — the Tensyl-X tendons have been swapped with a counterfeit that looks identical but snaps under load. Someone is selling fake TX cable in the Shelf, and people are dying.

A deep-salvage crew finds a cache of first-generation CNT cable from the 2080s — brittle, misaligned, but chemically exotic. A materials researcher is willing to pay obscene amounts for intact samples, and won't say why.
